userStories.title: Divergence tracker module (haircut expectation, halt logic)
userStories.description: As an operator, I want daily realized-vs-backtest divergence computed with an honest (haircut) expectation, alerting on drift and writing the breaker halt file on severe breach. [PRD US-009 part 1]
acceptanceCriteria: New execution/divergence.py: loads Alpaca portfolio history since promoted_at, loads promoted workspace's ret.pkl daily-return distribution; sigma from the full test window; expectation mu_adj = 0.5 * backtest mean (haircut factor configurable under a divergence: config section)
Computes trailing 20-trading-day realized return vs expected 20*mu_adj and z = (realized - 20*mu_adj) / (sigma * sqrt(20))

z < -2 posts a Slack warning with realized vs expected numbers and drawdown since promotion; z < -3 OR drawdown since promotion > backtest MDD * 1.25 writes the existing breaker halt file (same file execution/breaker.py checks) and posts a rotating_light Slack notice naming the trigger and the manual clear procedure
Fewer than 20 trading days since promotion: posts nothing, exits 0 (warmup)
Module never trades and never modifies state other than the halt file; failures post a Slack error notice (same pattern as rebalance/pred-refresh)
Tests cover: z-score math with haircut, alert threshold, halt threshold via z, halt threshold via drawdown, warmup, halt-file write
Typecheck passes (make check: ruff + pyright + pytest)
userStories.notes: execution/divergence.py: pure evaluate_divergence (haircut mu_adj, trailing-window z, drawdown vs |MDD|×tolerance, strict-< z thresholds / at-limit-passes drawdown) + loud load_backtest_stats + divergence: config section. Halt writes the breaker halt file (never overwrites an operator note); warmup/nothing-promoted silent. E2E on real account: warmup live, ok z=0.14 dd 2.83%/20.15% on a backdated DB copy, forced halt writes file + rotating_light.

userStories.title: GPU base-snapshot auto-use with rebake on drift
userStories.description: As an operator, I want Slack-launched runs to boot from the baked snapshot when current, and to rebuild it automatically when worker-affecting inputs change. [PRD US-019]
acceptanceCriteria: A worker-inputs hash is defined: short digest over research/PINNED_COMMIT, ops/gpu_worker/gpu_worker.sh, the Makefile venv/install targets, and a store schema/version marker; the hash is embedded in the snapshot name

At launch the pipeline selects the latest snapshot whose hash AND region both match: match boots from snapshot; no match runs full bootstrap and bakes a fresh hash-tagged snapshot at teardown (before destroy), pruning superseded snapshots keeping the latest 2
GpuBackend.launch plumbs this through so Slack-launched runs get it by default; run-start Slack message states 'booted from snapshot' or 'full bootstrap (inputs changed - rebaking)'
latest_snapshot_id in ops/gpu_worker/gpu_worker.sh becomes region-aware
Manual overrides --snapshot bake / --no-snapshot remain and are documented in the runbook; bake failure never fails the run (Slack warning only)
Tests (mocked doctl) cover: hash computation, match/mismatch selection, region-aware selection, prune-keep-2, launch-arg plumbing
Typecheck passes (make check: ruff + pyright + pytest)
userStories.notes: New ops/gpu_snapshot.py owns worker_inputs_hash (PINNED_COMMIT + gpu_worker.sh + Makefile venv targets + STRUCTURAL store marker), hash+region selection, prune-keep-2; name rdq-gpu-base-<hash>-<ts>. Pipeline selects per size-plan region at provision (no match = stock image, never stale snapshot) and auto-bakes at teardown before destroy (bake/selection failures degrade, never fail the run); run-start Slack states boot mode. gpu_worker.sh delegates select/hash/prune to the python module (region-aware latest_snapshot_id); --snapshot bake / --no-snapshot overrides documented in both runbooks. E2E vs real doctl: 0 base images, select empty exit 0, prune no-op; hash 07b012d45126.

userStories.title: Point-in-time ADV universe builder mode
userStories.description: As an operator, I want us_liquid membership computed per-date from trailing liquidity so backtests stop admitting names by today's liquidity retroactively. [PRD US-010 part 1]
acceptanceCriteria: data/make_universe.py gains a point-in-time mode (default for us_liquid): per ticker, membership spans are date ranges where trailing 20-day ADV >= threshold and price >= threshold, evaluated monthly with one-period entry/exit hysteresis
Output uses qlib's instruments span format (SYMBOL<TAB>START<TAB>END, multiple rows per symbol allowed)
Legacy last-window mode remains available behind a flag (used by frozen/promoted snapshots)
Tests cover: span computation from synthetic price/volume data, hysteresis prevents single-month churn, span-format output, legacy mode unchanged
Typecheck passes (make check: ruff + pyright + pytest)
userStories.notes: mode key (config.yaml us_liquid: pit; --mode CLI override) on make_universe: PIT = monthly first-trading-day evals of trailing ADV/raw price with one-period entry/exit hysteresis, span-format rows via new write_instrument_rows (legacy write_instruments_file wraps it); span ends clamp to the ticker's all.txt end; PIT without filters refuses. make_factor_source dedups span rows. E2E on a symlinked mirror of the live store: 589 tickers / 720 spans / 5s; every live member retained; live instruments/us_liquid.txt untouched (rollout = US-024).
